messages:
mira: quick question — i'm about to enable the new `model-prefetch` rollout for the /search route. we already have an org-level `prefetch_enabled` true for beta orgs. does route-level route:/search override org, or do we need to change model scope too? any guardrails to add?

ajay: route overrides org if explicitly set for that route. precedence is most-specific wins: model -> route -> project -> org. so if you set it at route, it should apply for requests hitting /search, unless a model-level flag is present for that exact model id.

mira: got it. curious about canary audiences — we want 10% canary for new model variant on /search. if org has a broader canary list, do we intersect or prefer route audience?

ajay: audience matching is evaluated at the same specificity level as the flag. so a route-level audience will be used for route-level flags. It does not auto-intersect with org audiences. think of it as: resolution finds the most-specific flag entry and uses its audience. if you want both, set explicit audiences or a union in the route flag config.

jess: small gotcha: our rollout system supports a "fallback_to_lower_scope" policy (defaults to true). if enabled, when a route-level flag is missing the system will fall back to project/org. but it only falls back for flag value; it won't merge audiences across scopes.

mira: thanks — where's the config snippet for route flag? want to include in PR.

ajay: paste example:
```
flag: prefetch_enabled
scope:
  route: "/search"
  audience: {percent: 10, include: ["canary-segment-2026"]}
value: true
policies:
  fallback_to_lower_scope: false
  auto_revert_on_error_rate: 0.05
```

kai: fyi ops: enable `auto_revert_on_error_rate` for the canary, otherwise we saw a noisy model deploy last month. rollout-bot can watch and open an incident if >5% error. ping @rollout-bot in PR.

rollout-bot: [automatic] monitoring hook attached to flag prefetch_enabled for route /search. will notify on >5% error or latency regressions. :robot_face:

jess: one more operational note — if the model artifact has a `model-scoped` flag entry, that will win over route. so to be safe, add a model-level noop entry for the new variant to explicitly inherit route behavior if desired.

mira: actionable for me: (1) create route-level flag config with audience union as needed, (2) set fallback_to_lower_scope=false, (3) enable auto_revert_on_error_rate=0.05, (4) add model-level noop entry if we want to lock behavior. i'll open PR and tag you all for review.

ajay: sounds good. when you create PR, include a quick snippet of expected resolution path and a test matrix: org-only, route-only, model-only, route+model. quick smoke in staging pls.

mira: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
